fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A strategy is evolutionarily stable if, once common, it cannot be invaded by any rare alternative strategy.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: I is an ESS iff for all J \ne I: E(I,I) > E(J,I), or E(I,I) = E(J,I) and E(I,J) > E(J,J); every ESS is an asymptotically stable rest point of the replicator dynamics (Taylor and Jonker 1978), not conversely

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: John Maynard Smith (1973) The Logic of Animal Conflict

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: an infinite, well-mixed population with pairwise interactions and asexual or clonal inheritance of strategies

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: the definition is exact, and the link to replicator dynamics is proved. Finite populations, mutation and genetic constraints can stop an ESS from being reached.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: I is an ESS iff for all J \ne I: E(I,I) > E(J,I), or E(I,I) = E(J,I) and E(I,J) > E(J,J); every ESS is an asymptotically stable rest point of the replicator dynamics (Taylor and Jonker 1978), not conversely

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: In a system with measurable payoffs (microbial public-goods strains, contest behaviour), estimate the payoff matrix and test that the predicted ESS composition resists experimental invasion by rare alternative strategies.
